standard_prerequisites.use: Turns restriction of a sheaf on X_etale to U_etale into pullback along a_{small}, and likewise for b.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localisation of the module of differentials on ringed sites
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Modules on Sites, Lemma labelled sites-modules-lemma-localize-differentials; invoked at lines 1003-1005
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes Omega_{X/Y}|_{U_etale} as the module of differentials of the map of sheaves of rings induced by a_{small} and f_{small}.

core_obligations: Replace restriction to U_etale by pullback along a_{small} (and similarly b_{small} for V), so that the statement becomes a computation with modules of differentials of maps of sheaves of rings (proof lines 999-1003).
Apply the localisation lemma on ringed sites to write Omega_{X/Y}|_{U_etale} as Omega_{O_{U_etale}/a_{small}^{-1} f_{small}^{-1} O_{Y_etale}} (proof lines 1003-1010).

Identify the sheaf of rings in the denominator: a_{small}^{-1} f_{small}^{-1} O_{Y_etale} = psi_{small}^{-1} b_{small}^{-1} O_{Y_etale} = psi_{small}^{-1} O_{V_etale} by commutativity of the given square, which is Omega_{U/V} by definition (proof lines 1011-1013).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the restriction along a_{small} and b_{small} as pullbacks (proof lines 999-1003).
Apply the localisation lemma for differentials on ringed sites and rewrite the coefficient sheaf of rings using the commutative diagram (proof lines 1004-1013).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a morphism of algebraic spaces f : X -> Y over a scheme S and a commutative square with etale vertical maps a : U -> X and b : V -> Y, and asserts the restriction formula Omega_{X/Y}|_{U_etale} = Omega_{U/V}, with the scheme case of the usual sheaf of differentials as a corollary (statement lines 980-996). The proof does not run through presentations of algebraic spaces at all: it identifies restriction to U_etale with pullback along a_{small} by the etale-topos equivalence, applies the localisation lemma for differentials on ringed sites, and then rewrites the coefficient sheaf of rings through the commutativity of the square (proof lines 999-1013). The step that carries the content is that last rewriting, because it is the only place where the hypothesis that the square commutes is used. The proof is short but has no gap and no omitted argument, so H2.
